text.p: Pen pictures of possible Bayern Munich team for Saturday's German first division match against VfB Stuttgart:

Oliver Kahn. Goalkeeper. Age 27. Germany's second-choice keeper who is ambitious to make a career in the national team. A big man who dominates the penalty area with both his stature, loud voice and aggression.

Lothar Matthaeus. Libero. 36. Germany's most capped player with 122 international appearances and a former World Cup captain. His international days are over and he is slower than in his heyday but still a player who can turn a match with a piece of skill. One goal this season.

Markus Babbel. Defender. 24. Euro 96 player who was tipped to be Juergen Kohler's successor as main man-to-man marker in national team but who has yet to match the Borussia Dortmund player's consistency. Two goals this season.

Thomas Helmer. Defender. 32. German international who operates mainly as a man marker for Bayern. He can also slot easily into the libero role. A calming influence on the side and one of its undisputed leadership figures. Four goals this season.

Mario Basler. Midfielder. 28. Joined from Werder Bremen at start of season. The German international has promised a great deal in recent seasons but injuries have often hindered his progress. Showing good form lately however. One of the country's most gifted players but his comments in public often get him into trouble. Eight goals this season.
Christian Nerlinger. Midfielder. 24. One of Bayern's rising stars who has been at the club since 1987 and who fits into the team well alongside the bigger names. Four goals to his credit this season.

Christian Ziege. Wing back. 25. Left-sided German international who has risen to prominence with a string of impresive displays for both Bayern and the national side. Will join AC Milan at the end of this season. Scored against Rostock last weekend, his sixth goal of the season.

Mehmet Scholl. Midfielder. 26. German Euro 96 player has struggled with injuries and failed to make a huge impact this season despite his talents. But returning to form. Scored in 3-0 win at Rostock last weekend, his fourth goal of season.

Alexander Zickler. Forward. 23. Former Dynamo Dresden player came under fire for lack of sharpness in front of goal when he was thrown into the team because of injuries two seasons ago but has matured into an intelligent player. Yet to be an automatic first-choice but seven goals this season.

Juergen Klinsmann. Forward. 32. Germany's captain and best known player has not enjoyed his two seasons at Bayern because of internal battles and defensive tactics. He is leaving to join Sampdoria in Italy at end of season but is still fired up to win his first German championship. Scored superb goal last weekend and is club's leading marksman with 14 goals this term.

Ruggeiro Rizzitelli. Forward. 29. Former Italian international had problems settling into the Bayern side when he joined from Torino at the start of the season. But he has been in brilliant form in the second half of the season, scoring goals himself and setting up chances for others. Six goals to his credit.
